---
title: "Choice Modelling"
description: "Discrete choice experiments, preference heterogeneity, and model interpretation."
---

## Overview

Choice modelling helps estimate how people make trade-offs between attributes such as cost, environmental quality, access, risk, and management options. I am especially interested in models that make preference heterogeneity interpretable and useful for policy analysis.

## Themes

- Choice experiment design and survey data preparation
- Multinomial logit, mixed logit, and latent class models
- Willingness-to-pay estimation
- Class membership covariates and heterogeneity
- Communicating model assumptions and uncertainty

## Tools

Common tools include R, Apollo, tidyverse workflows, Quarto reporting, and reproducible project structures.

## Related Work

See the [choice modelling toolkit project](../projects/choice-modelling-toolkit/) and future blog posts for applied examples.
